UEC European Championships 2026 Women’s Elite Road Race: Our form guide

The women’s elite road race at the European Championships takes place on Saturday 3rd October. The 130km route begins in Ljubljana and travels 85km north towards Šenčur for a 22.1km circuit featuring the Možjanca climb that will be undertaken twice.

Newly crowned World Champion Demi Vollering (Netherlands) unsurprisingly enters as favourite to defend her title, but a whole host of riders have flown from Canada to Slovenia to try and rain on her parade.

Demi Vollering (Netherlands)

Just one last task awaits the Netherlands’ Demi Vollering for 2026. Retain the European Championships jersey. Her chances are strong to say the least. While the Dutch rider has been crushingly strong this year, she did not win the recent World Championships with ease. Her planned solo breakaway was reeled back in and she had to battle a cramping Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney in the sprint.

This blip – and a strong chase group should she get away – might prove to be a thorn in her side should a similar fate occur in Slovenia, and with an easier parcours her competitors should have a better chance of keeping her from going clear.

Best finish in European Championship Elite Road Race

  • 1st: 2025

Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney (Poland)

Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney’s dogged determination to claw back Vollering almost landed her a rainbow jersey. She looked hungry, and a European Championship could be quite the prize for someone that narrowly missed out on a world title.

Vollering will be her biggest rival once again, as has been the case all season. Niewiadoma-Phinney finished second to her in the European Championships road race last season after Vollering’s 37km solo attack. It was her second silver medal at this race after 2016, when Anna van der Breggen bested her competitors in a sprint for the first title.

Elisa Longo Borghini (Italy)

The World Championships culminated in a bronze medal for Elisa Longo Borghini, as the podium matched that of the Tour de France Femmes. The Italian has occupied all sports of the podium aside from the top rung in the European Championships road race, finishing second in 2020 to Annemiek van Vleuten in a two-up sprint and third in the sprint in 2016.

Her aggressive racing and massive engine means she’s capable of winning any race she lines up at, but she’s only bested Vollering once all season.

Marlen Reusser (Switzerland)

Reusser had a brilliant time in Canada, with a dominant time-trial title defence and a mightily impressive fourth place after being instrumental in bringing Vollering back to the group. She had been caught out earlier on as Vollering attacked while she was back with her team car, who knows how the race would’ve played out had she been present.

Reusser is one of a few riders to have beaten Vollering in 2026, outsprinting her Dutch rival to win Dwars door Vlaanderen. Her TT ability means if – and it’s a big if – she manages to get solo it will be nigh-on impossible to catch her, but failing that she’ll be confident in a small group sprint.

Juliette Berthet (France)

France’s Juliette Berthet has had a solid season having spent most of the year in service of Vollering. When not on domestique duties, Berthet – formerly Labous – rode to fifth at La Vuelta Femenina, a podium at CIC-Tour Féminin des Pyrénées and won the Faun Tour Femmes in impressive fashion.

The French squad had three riders in the top ten in the World Championships road race with Juliette Berthet fifth, Célia Gery seventh and Maeva Squiban ninth, but they’d have been hoping for more. Gery won’t be riding in Slovenia, but Berthet is joined by Squiban and Cédrine Kerbaol in the race for the Euro bands.

Other riders to watch

Also vying for the last big jersey of the season will be the likes of Noemi Rüegg (Switzerland), who won the Tour Down Under. briefly led La Vuelta Femenina and had a series of strong placings in the Classics with second in Milan-San Remo, fifth at the Amstel Gold Race, seventh at Trofeo Oro and eighth at Trofeo Alfredo Binda. Paired with Reusser the Swiss team have a great chance of getting a big result.

Paris-Roubaix Femmes champion Franziska Koch (Germany) has enjoyed a good run of form lately too, podiuming the Classic Lorient Agglomération, finishing fourth in the Grand Prix Region Stuttgart, and coming third in the World Championships TT before a tenth place in the road race. She’s part of a strong German team that includes Tour white jersey winner Antonia Niedermaier and puncheur Liane Lippert.

Should Vollering wish for the European jersey to actually be worn in 2027, she could help in-form teammates Puck Pieterse, Femke De Vries or Karlijn Swinkels
